newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-EL GUERROUJ MUST AVOID TROUBLE TO WIN GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EL GUERROUJ MUST AVOID TROUBLE TO WIN GOLD.

text.p: Moroccan Hicham el Guerrouj will need to run away from trouble as well as his rivals in the men's 1,500 metres final on Wednesday, the blue riband event of the world championships.
At last year's Atlanta Olympics, the Moroccan's gold medal hopes disappeared after he tripped over rival Noureddine Morceli's foot while making a move to the front.
Despite being spiked Morceli went on to add the Olympic title to his three world golds.
When the two athletes clash on the Athens track, tactics will be as important as speed.
"Hicham is ready," said his personal coach, Abdelkader Kada. "Not only has he the ability to win the title but I think he can become one of the greatest middle distance runners of all time."
The Moroccan soon regained his composure after Atlanta, remaining undefeated in the 1,500 for the remainder of the season and beating Morceli in the Grand Prix final in Milan in September.
El Guerrouj looked just as awesome at the start of this year's outdoor season, clocking the three fastest times including a year's best of 3:29.30 last month in Stockholm.
Morceli had to work hard before winning his semifinal on Monday. Now 27, the Algerian he will have to produce one of the best runs of his life to clinch a fourth title.
Distance runners also take the stage on the fifth day of the championships with the finals of the 10,000 metres and the 3,000 metres steeplechase.
Ethiopia's world record holder Haile Gebrselassie, who originally did not want to come to the championships because he felt the track was too hard, is the favourite to take the 10,000.
Kenyan world record holder and defending champion Moses Kiptanui hopes to make up for the disappointment of just missing out on gold in Atlanta in the steeplechase.
